source.version: Working paper dated March 2, 2026 (title page and Web Appendix title page), from coauthor Artem Timoshenko's website; newer than the SSRN 5371575 posting of 2025. Printed page numbers run one behind PDF page numbers (printed p. 1 = PDF p. 2); Web Appendix page WA-n = PDF p. 44+n.
source.title_on_document: Guided Creativity: AI Intermediation for Enhancing Originality and Quality in Visual Design

supplement.where: Appendix A-E (printed pp. 35-43, PDF pp. 36-44) and Web Appendix A-D (WA-1 to WA-25, PDF pp. 45-69), both inside this PDF
supplement.holds: Full regression tables with designer-clustered standard errors: Tables WA-C.1 (quality), WA-C.2 (embedding originality), WA-C.3 and WA-C.4 (pairwise contrasts with SEs) for Study 1; Tables WA-D.2 to WA-D.5 for the restaurant replication; perception-based originality (Appendix C, Figure C.1); balance tables B.1 and WA-D.1; alignment Table E.3.

paper_design_summary: Professional freelance logo designers recruited on freelancer.com entered a real two-week logo design contest and were randomized at registration to see a gallery of 60 human logo exemplars with ratings (Open), no gallery (Blind), or a gallery of AI-generated variations of those exemplars made by the authors' fine-tuned FLUX.1-dev pipeline (one or four variations per exemplar). Submissions were scored on quality (survey-based click attractiveness) and originality (CLIP embedding distance, or survey-rated distance, to the 12 leading exemplars, among the top-50 quality submissions per condition). A second contest for a restaurant brand replicated the design with Open, Blind, and Variation(4) arms.

eligibility.reason: S1: professional designers randomized at registration to galleries of AI-generated logo variations versus no exemplars (Blind) or human exemplars (Open) in a real contest; 292 designers analyzed (440 registered), well above 50; quality (survey click attractiveness) and originality (CLIP distance to exemplars) scored on submitted logos. S2 replicates with 208 analyzed designers. The AI intervention is a researcher-generated gallery of AI examples (ideas_supplied), not free tool use.

one_line_finding: In a field logo contest with 292 participating designers, a gallery of AI-generated variations raised submission quality over no exemplars (Delta = 0.067, p = 0.001, about 13 percent) and matched human-exemplar quality (Delta = 0.002, p = 0.930), while top-50 submissions were more original than under human exemplars (Open minus Variation = -0.014, p = 0.008) and as original as Blind (p = 0.516) (printed pp. 22-23, Figures 6-7; Tables WA-C.1 to WA-C.4).
open_questions: Should a researcher-curated gallery of AI-generated examples (participants never operate the AI) count as 'generative-AI assistance' under criterion 1? It fits the codebook's ideas_supplied role.

Originality is distance from the 12 leading exemplars, not similarity across participants, so the paper has no across_people diversity outcome even though it frames the result as reducing fixation and homogenization.
Originality is computed only on the top-50 quality submissions per condition, a post-treatment selection; which designers contribute those submissions is not reported.

Registered designers are treated as randomized (Figure 4 notes say randomization happened upon registration); 34 to 37 percent of each arm never submitted in S1 and 53 to 60 percent in S2, so analyses are not intention-to-treat.
notes: Whole PDF read (69 pages, main text, Appendix A-E, Web Appendix A-D). Retrieval record lists 'Kellogg' as a fourth author; the document has three authors (Wu, Aridor, Timoshenko) and Kellogg is their school. All main estimates are submission-level regressions with designer-clustered SEs and designer controls (reputation, professionalism, hire again, quality, number of jobs, reviews, hourly rate) plus submission day. The Variation(4) arm of S1 is in the regressions (N = 2199 and 200 include it) but its coefficient is printed only as bars in Figure 9. Figure 9 and Figure 10 notes swap the panel descriptions relative to the panel titles (titles say A = Originality, B = Quality). Not listed as outcomes because they answer none of the three questions: (a) top-50 Variation submissions versus professionally refined AI variations, originality Delta = 0.017, p < 0.001 and quality Delta = 0.295, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 28, Figure 10; refinement designers' count not stated); (b) model-only validation studies of the variations (Web Appendix B.3: alignment, dispersion of variations vs exemplars, Optimization LoRA click test with survey participants). Quality ratings were also fed back to designers during the contest: 10 random submissions per condition were rated daily and the ratings sent privately (PDF pp. 18-20).
